data: First Starship orbital flight test; designed for the full reusable Mars-bound stack

Starship launch pad at Boca Chica / Starbase, Texas, 26°N. First integrated Starship flight test (IFT-1) on April 20, 2023 — vehicle lost ~4 minutes after liftoff following engine failures, but the pad survived. Subsequent IFTs have demonstrated booster catch via the Mechazilla tower arms and increasing test-flight success across 2024-2025. Designed for the fully reusable Mars-bound Starship + Super Heavy stack at unprecedented cadence; the pad's water deluge system is the largest deployed for any orbital launch system. Coordinates from FAA + SpaceX public records.

SpaceX's Starship pad at Boca Chica, Texas — built from scratch starting in 2019 for the fully reusable Starship + Super Heavy. First integrated flight test (IFT-1) lifted off April 20, 2023; vehicle lost ~4 minutes post-liftoff after engine failures caused loss of control, but the pad survived. Subsequent IFTs through 2024-25 demonstrated booster catch via the Mechazilla tower arms, successful sea splashdowns, and increasing payload-class capability. The water deluge system at this pad is the largest ever built for an orbital launch — the over-pressure footprint from 33 Raptor-class engines is unlike anything else flying.
